system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: SYCL reduction library

ATOM DPCPP2-C05-S3-02 (S3): SYCL implementations can automatically determine the correct identity value only when the reduction operates on simple arithmetic types and uses one of several standard function objects such as plus, so user-defined reductions may improve performance by specifying the identity value directly.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0388-s07] SYCL implementations can only automatically determine the correct
[DPCPP2-p0388-s08] identity value to use when a reduction is operating on simple arithmetic types and the reduction operator is one of several standard function objects (e.g., plus).
[DPCPP2-p0388-s09] For user-defined reductions (i.e., those operating on user-defined types and/or using user-defined function objects), we may be able to improve performance by specifying the identity value directly.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Automatic identity determination restrictions and potential performance improvement from specifying an identity are separate claims. / Joins two claims: when identity values are automatically determined, and how user-defined reductions can improve performance.
- L1_ONLY: revise — Separate the automatic-identity restriction from the performance recommendation; the latter adds evaluative load. / Stacked conditions and optimization advice; split or drop the performance clause.
raw: {"atoms": [{"statement": "SYCL implementations can only automatically determine the correct identity value for a reduction when it operates on simple arithmetic types and its operator is one of several standard function objects (e.g., plus).", "scope": "S3", "evidence_ids": ["DPCPP2-p0388-s07", "DPCPP2-p0388-s08"]}, {"statement": "For user-defined reductions (those using user-defined types and/or user-defined function objects), performance may be improved by specifying the identity value directly.", "scope": "S2", "evidence_ids": ["DPCPP2-p0388-s09"]}], "note": "Split the original into the automatic-identity restriction and the performance-improvement claim; the 'may' hedge is retained."}
